Name: Meikyoku Kissa Violon
Hours: Roughly 12:00-17:00/18:00 record time, live music evenings; closed Tuesdays (closing time differs by source)
Address (JA): 東京都杉並区阿佐谷北2-9-5
Notes: Small, intimate classical listening café in a house on a quiet lane, about 300m from JR Asagaya; around since 1980. Vinyl in the afternoon, occasional live music in the evening. Entry about ¥500 including coffee; closed Tuesdays. Reviewers find it quieter and less touristy than Lion.

Name: Koga Shoten
Address (JA): ~東京都千代田区神田神保町2丁目
Notes: Used bookshop in the Jimbocho book district specializing in classical scores, composer biographies and music theory. Great for browsing out-of-print editions.

Name: Yamaha Ginza
Hours: 11:00-18:30 (unclear if whole store); closed Tuesdays unless a holiday
Notes: 14-floor Yamaha flagship with a large sheet music selection. The ground-floor "Key Between People" piano is free for anyone to play, no reservation. Yamaha Hall (333 seats, all wood) holds concerts; check its calendar for your dates. Update: Yamaha Hall is on 7F.

Name: Academia Music
Notes: Known as Tokyo's specialist for imported classical scores (Henle, Bärenreiter and others). Details unverified, so check hours before going. Update: Search gave no address. Location approximate: pinned near 本郷三丁目 station until the shop is found.

Name: Sumida Triphony Hall
Hours: Dec 17 (Christmas concert) and Dec 18 (family concert) per the line
Notes: December is "Daiku" (Beethoven's 9th) season in Japan. NJP with Yutaka Sado: Dec 17 Sumida Triphony (Christmas concert), Dec 18 Sumida family concert, Dec 21 Tokyo Opera City. Dec 19 (Suntory Hall) and Dec 20 are sold out. Update: Only the Dec 19 Suntory Hall performance was verified; Dec 17/18/21 were not on njp.or.jp (its listings only reached Nov 28).

Name: Tokyo Opera City Concert Hall
Notes: December is "Daiku" (Beethoven's 9th) season in Japan. NJP with Yutaka Sado: Dec 17 Sumida Triphony (Christmas concert), Dec 18 Sumida family concert, Dec 21 Tokyo Opera City. Dec 19 (Suntory Hall) and Dec 20 are sold out. Update: Only the Dec 19 Suntory Hall performance was verified; Dec 17/18/21 were not on njp.or.jp (its listings only reached Nov 28).

Name: Francois Kissashitsu
Address (JA): 京都府京都市下京区西木屋町通四条下ル船頭町184
Notes: Historic 1934 café with a ship-cabin baroque interior, playing classical music; a registered cultural property. An easy stop downtown. Update: Cash only (no cards), per listings.

Name: Meikyoku Kissa Ryugetsudo
Address (JA): ~京都府京都市左京区田中上柳町
Notes: Lion-style silent listening room with a huge record library; you request pieces by writing the catalog number. Has a harpsichord and piano. Extra ¥500 music charge on top of drinks; closed Tuesdays. Details from a 2015 list, so check hours.

Name: Ongaku Kissa Musik
Notes: 15-seat café opened in 1987 by a former classical agency staffer; Tannoy speakers and a turntable that plays SP records (old 78s); siphon coffee. Open only Mon–Thu 13:00–18:00, so plan around it.

Name: Montage
Notes: Baroque and classical records with a harpsichord and piano on site; hosts concerts, and on some rehearsal days the café runs alongside them. Closed Fridays. Details from a 2015 list, so check current status. Location approximate: pinned near 二条城前 station until the shop is found.

Name: JEUGIA Sanjo Honten
Notes: Kyoto's main music store: sheet music and music books on 2F, pianos on 4F, CDs and records on 1F. Tax-free shopping. 5 minutes from Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Station. Location approximate: pinned near 京都市役所前 station until the shop is found.

Name: Shimamura Music Grand Front Osaka
Notes: Large sheet music section: classical and imported piano scores, orchestral pocket scores, theory books and composer biographies. Right by Osaka Station.
